staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this local vulnerable checkout. Local blame still shows the unfixed `if (++dos > 1)` cap check at line 215, and the saved AddressSanitizer stack names the same `src/bmffimage.cpp` lines present in this snapshot.

classification_note: ARVO metadata labels this sample `CWE-125`, but the saved ASan report and the staged source both show a container-overflow WRITE caused by shrinking the output buffer below the already-produced byte count, so this GT classifies it as `CWE-787`.

bug_description.original: Crash Type: Container-overflow WRITE {*} Crash State: libbrotlidec.so.1 BrotliDecoderDecompressStream Exiv2::BmffImage::brotliUncompress Sanitizer: address (ASAN)
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 65577-byte BMFF witness is accepted by Exiv2 and reaches `Exiv2::BmffImage::boxHandler()` on a root box whose header bytes at file offset `0x1c` are `00 00 00 00 62 72 6f 62`. Exiv2 therefore interprets the box as zero-length `brob`, extends it to EOF, and materializes a 65541-byte payload. The `TAG_brob` case strips the first 4 payload bytes and calls `brotliUncompress(data.c_data(4), data.size() - 4, arr)`, so `compressedBufSize` becomes 65537 and `uncompressedLen` starts at 131074. After the first `BrotliDecoderDecompressStream()` needs more output, vulnerable code doubles `uncompressedLen`, hits its 128 KiB cap, and then forces `uncompressedLen = 131072` without the later-added `total_out > 131072` guard. The saved ASan allocation/crash addresses, together with the vulnerable branch and the fix hunk, establish the narrower load-bearing state that by the next iteration `total_out` already exceeds 131072 before bounds are recomputed. As a result, `available_out = uncompressedLen - total_out` underflows and `next_out = arr.data() + total_out` points past the resized logical buffer. The second `BrotliDecoderDecompressStream()` then writes through that invalid output window, and Stage 01 reproduces an AddressSanitizer container-overflow WRITE of size 65534 with top project frame `Exiv2::BmffImage::brotliUncompress` at `src/bmffimage.cpp:208`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the crashing box header. `boxHandler()` reads the next 8 attacker-controlled bytes into `hdrbuf`; later steps parse those bytes as the zero-length root `brob` header that selects the vulnerable Brotli path.
source.value_from: The staged PoC at `gt_results/arvo_61675/poc` is 65577 bytes (sha256 `ae56107847098404b6a3cb810a280e7856cd63ecfa68ea40bdfd3bbd8b8d8e03`). At file offset `0x1c`, its next 8 bytes are `00 00 00 00 62 72 6f 62`, so this read loads the exact header later parsed as `box_length == 0` and `box_type == TAG_brob`.
source.note: This is the scored source rather than `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` because it is the first project parser statement that reads the specific box header governing the vulnerable path.

sink.description: Crash-adjacent sink. The second Brotli call consumes the wrapped `available_out` and the `next_out` pointer computed past the resized `DataBuf`, so libbrotli writes beyond the container.
sink.note: The saved ASan report shows `WRITE of size 65534` in `__interceptor_memcpy` / `BrotliDecoderDecompressStream`, with `Exiv2::BmffImage::brotliUncompress` at `src/bmffimage.cpp:208:9` as the top project frame.

root_cause.description: Missing bounds check in the DoS-cap branch. On the first cap hit, vulnerable code only checks `++dos > 1` and therefore allows `uncompressedLen` to be reset to 131072 even when `total_out` already exceeds that cap.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes this condition to `if (++dos > 1 || total_out > 131072)`, confirming that the missing `total_out > 131072` guard is what prevents the later arithmetic underflow and out-of-bounds output pointer.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled `brob` payload becomes the Brotli input slice here. For the staged witness, `data.size() - 4` is 65537, and that exact size is later doubled, capped, and subtracted from `total_out` on the crashing path.
tainted_value_origin.note: Step 6 materializes the 65541-byte payload; this call strips the first 4 payload bytes and forwards the remaining bytes as the compressed buffer used in `brotliUncompress()`.

parser_admitted.description: After `openOrThrow()` accepts the witness as BMFF, `readMetadata()` begins root-box traversal and enters the `boxHandler()` instance that parses the root `brob` header instead of rejecting the file earlier.

evidence_limitations: Runtime disambiguation was disabled by `run_flags.json`, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation or rerun the target beyond the saved Stage 01 artifacts.
Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image or patch, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains `false`; the fix effect is source-grounded from `patch.diff` only.

The saved artifacts do not establish the exact `total_out` value before the second call; they only close the load-bearing inequality `total_out > 131072` before the vulnerable code recomputes `available_out` and `next_out`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness opens the attacker-controlled bytes as an Exiv2 image and calls `readMetadata()`.
Exiv2 accepts the file as BMFF, reads a root box header `00 00 00 00 62 72 6f 62`, interprets it as zero-length `brob`, and materializes a 65541-byte payload.
The `TAG_brob` branch strips the first 4 payload bytes, forwards 65537 compressed bytes to Brotli, and sizes the first output buffer as `compressedBufSize * 2 = 131074`.
After the first Brotli call returns `NEEDS_MORE_OUTPUT`, vulnerable cap logic doubles `uncompressedLen`, then caps it to 131072 without checking whether `total_out` already exceeds that value.

The next loop iteration computes an underflowed `available_out` and a `next_out` pointer beyond the resized buffer, and the second `BrotliDecoderDecompressStream()` produces the saved container-overflow write.

fine_trace.note: Source. While traversing root boxes, `boxHandler()` reads the next 8 attacker-controlled bytes into `hdrbuf`. For the triggering root box at file offset `0x1c`, these bytes are `00 00 00 00 62 72 6f 62`, the header later parsed as a zero-length `brob` box.
The first four header bytes decode to `box_length == 0`, the BMFF sentinel meaning that this box extends to EOF.
The next four header bytes decode to `TAG_brob`, so the later switch dispatches this root box to the Brotli metadata case.
Because step 2 produced zero length, `boxHandler()` rewrites `box_length` to the remaining file size from offset `0x1c` to EOF. For the 65577-byte witness, the box length becomes 65549 bytes.
Subtracting the 8-byte root header yields a `brob` payload size of 65541 bytes.
The entire zero-length `brob` payload is materialized in `data`. These bytes become the metadata buffer used by the `TAG_brob` branch.
Entering the `TAG_brob` case, Exiv2 strips the first 4 payload bytes as `realType` and passes the remaining 65537 bytes to Brotli as `compressedBuf` and `compressedBufSize`.

fine_trace.code: size_t uncompressedLen = compressedBufSize * 2;  // just a starting point
fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled compressed size from step 7 is 65537, so the starting output length is 131074 bytes. This is already 2 bytes above the later 128 KiB cap value of 131072.
On the first loop iteration `total_out` is still 0, so Exiv2 allocates a 131074-byte `DataBuf`, exposes the full buffer as `available_out`, and points `next_out` at its beginning.

The first Brotli call does not finish and returns `BROTLI_DECODER_RESULT_NEEDS_MORE_OUTPUT`. The saved ASan write at the end of the original 131074-byte allocation, together with the later-added `total_out > 131072` guard, establish that before the next loop recomputes bounds `total_out` already exceeds 131072. The exact value is not logged.
Handling `NEEDS_MORE_OUTPUT` doubles `uncompressedLen` from 131074 to 262148. That doubled value is what trips the DoS-cap predicate on the same path.

Root cause. On the first cap hit, vulnerable code only tests `++dos > 1`; because `dos` goes from 0 to 1, that condition is false, so execution continues and forces `uncompressedLen` down to 131072 without checking the patch's missing condition `total_out > 131072`. Step 10 has already established that `total_out` exceeds the cap, so this branch makes the target size smaller than the data already emitted.
The next loop iteration resizes `arr` down to 131072 bytes even though `total_out` from the previous call already exceeds 131072.

Using step 12's capped length and step 10's produced-byte count, Exiv2 subtracts a larger `total_out` from `uncompressedLen = 131072`. Because `available_out` is `size_t`, this subtraction underflows and wraps to a huge positive length instead of stopping the loop.
The same `total_out > 131072` also moves `next_out` past the end of the now-131072-byte logical buffer.

Sink. The second Brotli call consumes the wrapped `available_out` and the out-of-bounds `next_out`, so libbrotli writes through an invalid output window. ASan reports this as a 65534-byte container-overflow write, with the faulting `memcpy` destination at the end of the original 131074-byte vector allocation and `src/bmffimage.cpp:208` as the top project frame.

depends_on.via: `++dos > 1` is false on the first cap hit, so execution continues with `uncompressedLen = 131072`.

allocation_context.note: ASan identifies the overflowing container as the 131074-byte vector allocation triggered by `arr.alloc(uncompressedLen)` on the first loop iteration.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Partially. The saved ASan top frame is `__interceptor_memcpy` inside libbrotli, and the recorded sink at `src/bmffimage.cpp:208` is the top project frame that supplies the wrapped length and out-of-bounds output pointer to that write.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the vulnerability by running `docker exec gt-arvo_61675-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'` with this file mounted as `/tmp/poc`, which drives `fuzz-read-print-write` to the saved AddressSanitizer crash in `Exiv2::BmffImage::brotliUncompress`.

format.name: BMFF / MP4 Base Media
format.contract: Exactly the staged 65577-byte witness in `gt_results/arvo_61675/poc` (sha256 `ae56107847098404b6a3cb810a280e7856cd63ecfa68ea40bdfd3bbd8b8d8e03`). Its root box at offset `0x1c` begins with header bytes `00 00 00 00 62 72 6f 62`, so `boxHandler()` interprets a zero-length `brob` box extending to EOF. That makes the `brob` payload size 65541 and the Brotli input length `data.size() - 4` equal 65537. Those exact values make `uncompressedLen` start at 131074, make the first `NEEDS_MORE_OUTPUT` path later cap `uncompressedLen` down to 131072, and on the saved crashing path leave `total_out` already above that cap before `available_out = uncompressedLen - total_out` is recomputed. Stage 01 only proves this exact witness and observed arithmetic; it does not generalize to other box layouts or nearby sizes.
